# Writing Style \- V1

# Writing Style \- Context v1 

# **Summary**

Content Studio's agents are only as good as the brand context they're given. **Writing Style** is where that context lives \- voice, audience, per-article-type conventions, and style standards — and it feeds directly into Content Creator at generation time. Without it, every draft starts cold and reads generically. With it, the agent writes in the brand's voice, for a named audience, in the brand's preferred format, without the user re-briefing it every time.

Writing Style has four components: Brand Voice, Audience, Article Type Preferences, and Style Preferences.

## **Overall User Flow**

1. Context Landing Page shows three cards \- Brand Kit, Writing Style, Knowledge Base.  
2. The user clicks the Writing Style card and lands on a detail page listing the four components.  
3. The user configures each component independently. None block the others \- a user can leave any incomplete and still use the rest.  
4. Configuration persists to the Context data store. Unconfigured components show an empty state with a prompt to fill them in.  
5. When the user later builds content in Content Creator, Content builder auto-loads Writing Style data: Brand Voice, the matching Article Type preference, and the selected Style standard apply automatically. If Brand Voice is unset, the agent asks for it inline during generation instead of blocking the flow.  
6. The user can override any Writing Style value per content piece from inside Content Creator, without changing the saved Context default.

# **1\. Brand Voice**

**User Story:** As a Content Creator, I want Gravton to understand my brand's tone, so every generated draft sounds like us without manual editing.

**Mechanics:** An upload zone accepts documents, URLs, or pasted text up to 3 to 4 content samples. On upload, the system extracts and displays a **tone summary** (e.g., "Professional, data-driven"), a **voice type** (Active or Passive), and **key vocabulary patterns**. The user can edit any extracted value. Before any samples are uploaded, the component shows an empty state: "Upload content samples to train your brand voice."

**Acceptance Criteria:**

* Upload zone accepts documents, URLs, and pasted text as input formats.  
* The system extracts tone summary, voice type, and vocabulary patterns from 3-4 samples.  
* All extracted fields are user-editable and persist on save.  
* Empty state renders before the first upload.

**Boundaries:**

* Extraction is LLM-driven. On failure or low-confidence extraction, fallback to manual input with four presets: Professional, Conversational, Technical, Casual.  
* Ships P0.

**Dependencies:**

* Content Creator reads Brand Voice at generation time; if unset, the agent asks for it inline rather than blocking generation.  
* LLM extraction pipeline for tone/voice-type classification.

# **2\. Audience**

**User Story:** As a Marketing Manager, I want to define my target audience profiles, so the Content Engine tailors messaging to specific segments.

**Mechanics:** An "Add Audience" action creates a new group. Each group captures Name, Pain Points, Communication Preferences, Technical Knowledge Level (Low/Medium/High), and Decision-Making Factors. Multiple groups are supported. One group is marked default and auto-applies in Content Creator unless overridden. Each group supports edit and delete.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

* User can create one or more audience groups via "Add Audience."  
* Each group captures all five fields listed above.  
* One group is marked default; Content Creator applies it automatically.  
* Content Creator surfaces an audience selector whenever more than one group exists.  
* Edit and delete are available per group.

**Boundaries:**

* No maximum group count is stated in this version of the spec. Flagged below.

**Dependencies:**

* Content Creator audience selection and default application happen here.

# **3\. Article Type Preferences**

**User Story:** As a Content Creator, I want to set preferences per article type, so blogs, guides, and comparisons each follow our established conventions.

**Mechanics:** The component lists all seven article types Gravton supports: Blogs, How-To Guides, Listicles, Comparisons, Technical Articles, Product Reviews, and Product Descriptions. Each type expands into a single free-text field for preferences or context — for example, "Blogs should always open with a data point. Avoid first-person." The list renders with empty fields by default and is fully functional unconfigured.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

* All seven article types render as independently expandable rows.  
* Each row carries one free-text preference field.  
* The component works with zero configuration  
* Selecting an article type in Content Creator injects the matching saved preference text into generation.

**Boundaries:**

* No character or word limit is stated for the preference field  
* Preferences are freeform text with no conditional logic. The Context PRD's scope explicitly excludes a rule engine (e.g., "if article type is Legal, apply Bluebook"). Rules are global defaults with per-piece override in Creator.

**Dependencies:**

* Content Creator article type selection triggers preference injection.

# **4\. Style Preferences**

**User Story:** As a Content Creator, I want to specify our writing style standard, so generated content follows AP Style, Chicago, or our industry format.

**Mechanics:** A dropdown or tag selector offers five style standards: AP Style, Chicago, MLA, APA, and Technical (IEEE, Bluebook, AMA). Single-select is the default state. The user can override the selection per content piece from within Content Creator. The selected standard displays as a label on the Writing Style summary view.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

* Selector offers all five listed style standards.  
* Single selection applies as the account default.  
* User can override the standard per content piece in Content Creator.  
* Selected standard renders as a label on the Writing Style summary.  
* Content Creator enforces the selected standard at generation time, not just at the label level.

**Boundaries:**

* No custom or freeform style-standard entry.

**Dependencies:**

* Content Creator references the selected standard during draft generation.

# Knowledge Base \- V1

# Knowledge Base \- Context v1 

# **Summary**

The core premise of Gravton's opportunity engine today is externally derived intelligence. The LLM sweeps, competitor tracking, GSC data, community signals. The gap is that it doesn't know what a brand actually *knows about its own customers.* This is what knowledge base solves. When Digit's internal data flows into Gravton, the opportunity engine stops making educated guesses about what customers care about and what are the guidelines and policies. 

This document highlights the product scope for Knowledge Base – A space for users to upload and manage brand owned content and declare the context and usages of the documents. Our system utilizes these documents to build opportunities, and content articles.

# **Overall Flow**

1. Knowledge Base is part of the Context Pages in the Actions panel. 

2. Users can create “Context Folders” and upload the documents here. Documents are ingested through File uploads (CSV, XSLS, CSV, DOCX, Web links, Pasting Content)  and API connectors (Google Drive). User uploaded documents from the following methods are also collected, and allotted to the “Sessions” (used once, never global) or “Library”(global standards) folder in the Page \- this allocation is made by the user. 

   1. Documents uploaded from the Onboarding (Connectors & Catalogue stage)  
   2. Documents uploaded as sources in the Content Studio sessions.   
      

3. **Context Folders.** Users create context folders to group documents together under a single context. Users can name and define the purpose of the folder during the creation. Contents from one folder can be moved to another folder and, name and purpose of the folder can be edited. Nesting folders is not in scope.

4. **Document Upload.** Users can upload their documents (CSV, XSLS, CSV, DOCX, Web links, Pasting Content)  or through API connectors (Google Drive). 

   1. **Process.** Each document upload must include **Context** \- where the user specifies what this document is about, **Folder** \- on which existing or new folder this document belongs in, **Usage** \- Is this document a Directive (global use), Reference (context document), Sessions Only (one time scope). 

   2. **Functions.** Documents can be uploaded, replaced \- if the exact named document is uploaded again, or deleted/removed. 

   3. **Freshness.** Each document carries with it the Uploaded time. This time is updated if documents are reuploaded. We surface a warning icon on documents after 6 months of no modifications.

5. The Context folders and documents along with their context statements are utilized by our system in the following ways, but not limited to

   1. Opportunity engine, to understand brand documents and research and insights and build brand tailored opportunities from the knowledge base. 

   2. Content Studio (More Strictly) to follow their writing standards and principles, guardrails and policies and compliance across all the content output. 

6. **Product Experience.** During the first interaction with this page. We create two blank context folders \- Policy & Guardrails, and Content Guidelines. *This nudges users to fill the two important context documents for our model, and also engage with the Context Folders feature.* 

# KB \- Data Sources

# **How do Sources look like**

## **1\. Product & Policy** *\- helps in brand kit, opportunity & content studio*

**What it is:** The canonical source of truth on what a brand sells, how it's structured, what's covered, what's excluded, and how it's priced.

**Specific data sources:**

* Policy wording documents (PDFs, Word docs) : per product line (motor, health, travel, home, commercial)  
* Product comparison sheets (XLS/PDF) : feature matrices across plans and competitors  
* Premium calculator inputs and outputs:  what variables drive price, at what ranges  
* Rider/add-on catalogs : structured list of add-ons with eligibility and pricing  
* Product FAQs : maintained internally, often in a CMS or internal wiki  
* Underwriting guidelines (where shareable) : what gets accepted, declined, or referred

**Integration modality:**

* File upload (PDF, DOCX, XLSX) for static documents at onboarding  
* CMS API integration (Contentful, Notion, Confluence) for living documents  
* Periodic re-ingestion trigger (monthly or on policy revision cycles)

### ***What this unlocks in Gravton:***

* The Brand Kit becomes structurally accurate: Gravton knows Digit sells "0-day cashless claims" not just "health insurance"  
* Opportunity engines can identify gaps between what Digit's product actually does vs. how LLMs describe it.   
* Content Studio can generate policy-specific content that references real coverage terms, not generic insurance copy

## **2\. Brand & Content Asset** *\- helps in Content studio grounding & compliance guardrails*

**What it is:** Everything Brand has already produced — their accumulated institutional content knowledge.

**Specific data sources:**

* Blog posts and articles (published and draft)  
* Campaign copy — taglines, hero messaging, key value propositions per product  
* Brand guidelines document — tone, voice, do/don't list, terminology rules  
* Press releases and media kit  
* Agent training manuals — how Digit explains its products to its own sales force  
* Social media content calendar and past posts  
* Email sequences — onboarding, claims, renewal campaigns

**Integration modality:**

* File upload (DOCX, PDF, CSV) at onboarding  
* Website crawl (already exists in Gravton) — but this extends it to gated/internal assets  
* Google Drive integration — if Digit stores content assets in Google Drive, a Drive connector can pull documents on a defined sync cadence

### ***What this unlocks in Gravton:***

* Brand voice calibration becomes precise — Content Studio generates drafts that match Digit's actual tone, not an approximated version  
* The compliance cage can reference Digit's own terminology rules — flagging if generated content uses phrases Digit has officially deprecated or prohibited  
* Existing content inventory feeds the "content exists but isn't earning citation" opportunity classification

## **3\. Performance & Attribution Data *\-*** *(High Trust Item) helps in Attribution, Enrich insights engine & Opportunity Generation*

**What it is:** How Brand’s existing digital presence actually performs — what gets traffic, what converts, what customers click from LLM responses.

**Specific data sources:**

* Google Search Console (already supported in Gravton): queries, impressions, CTR, position  
* Google Analytics 4 : page-level traffic, session source, conversion events  
* App analytics:  DAU/MAU by feature, drop-off points in the purchase journey  
* Paid campaign data (Google Ads, Meta Ads): keyword performance, audience signals  
* Landing page conversion rates: by product, by campaign, by audience segment  
* Email performance data: open rates, click rates by content type

**Integration modality:**

* GSC: already in Gravton roadmap — priority integration  
* GA4: API integration (OAuth-based) — reads session and conversion data  
* App analytics: export via Mixpanel/Amplitude CSV, or API if available  
* Paid data: Google Ads API or exported CSV

**What this unlocks in Gravton:**

* Opportunity scoring gets a conversion layer \- a gap on a prompt that drives 40% of Digit's trial conversions is ranked orders of magnitude higher than a gap on an informational topic  
* The presence matrix gets grounded in actual traffic \- "winning" in LLMs is mapped against "converting" in Digit's own funnel  
* Attribution becomes meaningful — Gravton can start correlating LLM visibility shifts with GA4 traffic movement.

## **4\. Structured Product & Catalogue** *\- helps in shopping feature, LOB Mapper \-\> Prompt Enrichment, Content Studio*

**What it is:** Machine-readable product data — the kind insurers use to power their own calculators, APIs, and partner feeds.

**Specific data sources:**

* Product taxonomy XML/JSON (if Digit exposes an internal product API)  
* Premium rate tables (XLS) — by age band, sum insured, geography, plan type  
* Claim settlement ratio data — Digit publishes this publicly but may have richer internal cuts  
* Hospital/garage/partner network lists — structured CSV or API  
* Regulatory filings — IRDAI-approved policy wordings, tariff structures

**Integration modality:**

* File upload (XLS, CSV, JSON) for structured data  
* Internal API integration for live product catalog (if Digit's tech team can provide a read-only API endpoint)  
* Regulatory document ingestion (PDF parser)

**What this unlocks in Gravton:**

* The product vertical mapper is populated with actual SKUs and product structures — not just web-crawled approximations  
* LLM responses about Digit can be fact-checked against the canonical product data — this is the accuracy layer  
* Content Studio can inject real data points ("97.4% claim settlement ratio," "6,500+ network hospitals") into generated content automatically

# KB v1 \- Backlog

## **P1/P2 SCOPE \- FEATURES**

1. **Standards.** The extracted standards from the user uploaded documents, which dictate how to use specifics from the document, are visible to the users. Users see transparently what standard model has extracted and tagged it as.  
   

| Type | Definition | Example (Kestrel) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Fact** | A value that is true. Content must state it correctly or not at all. | Free shipping is $75 US / $120 CA. Warranty is 3 years hard goods, 1 year apparel. |
| **Prohibition** | Something content must never contain. Failure is the presence of something. | Never say "waterproof" without IP certification. Never claim a competitor product is discontinued without a linked announcement. |
| **Rule** | Something content must do or include. Failure is the absence of something. | Any mention of the 90-day return window must link to /returns and name the bundle restocking fee. |
| **Voice** | How writing should read. Shapes wording, never truth or legality. | Second person. Sentences under 22 words. Never "unlock", "elevate", "game-changing". |
| **Approval** | A named human must sign off before publish. Not a content constraint — a routing instruction. | Cold-weather safety claims route to Product Compliance. |

![][image1]

2. **Conflict on Knowledge.** If two or more conflicting standards or knowledge pieces are detected by the model. We find the resolutions, where human approval corrects which standard to maintain and keep. This helps brand knowledge to resolve conflicts and make better judgements. 

**![][image2]**

3. **Context Coverage.** We map out the missing/reinforceable brand information required by our agents to build better opportunities and content pieces for the brand. These are listed out in the Knowledge base, as Context Coverage we require from the Brand.
